  0 < n →
    Function.Injective ⇑f →
      Set.range ⇑f = ↑(AddSubgroup.torsionBy (AddCircle p) ↑n) → ∀ {u : H}, f u = ↑(p / ↑n) → ∀ (x : H), ∃ k, k • u = x
docstring:
The element of invariant `p / n` generates a group carrying an invariant map onto the
`n`-torsion.
description: **Cyclicity of the Preimage of the $n$-Torsion Subgroup of an Additive Circle.** Let $p$ be a positive element of a strictly ordered field and let $\mathbb{T}_p$ denote the additive circle of period $p$. For any positive integer $n$, let $f: H \to \mathbb{T}_p$ be an injective group homomorphism from an additive group $H$ such that the range of $f$ is exactly the $n$-torsion subgroup of $\mathbb{T}_p$. If $u \in H$ is an element such that $f(u) = p/n \pmod p$, then $H$ is a cyclic group generated by $u$; that is, every element $x \in H$ can be written as an integer multiple $k \cdot u$ for some $k \in \mathbb{Z}$.

description: **Homotopy between the contraction idempotent and the identity.** For any contraction $c$ between cochain complexes $K$ and $L$ in a preadditive category, there exists a homotopy between the idempotent endomorphism $i \circ p$ on $K$ induced by the contraction and the identity morphism on $K$.

name: TauCeti.IsGradedExtComparison
signature:
structure TauCeti.IsGradedExtComparison : {C : Type u} →
  [inst : CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] →
    [inst_1 : CategoryTheory.Abelian C] →
      {D : Type u'} →
        [inst_2 : CategoryTheory.Category.{v', u'} D] →
          [inst_3 : CategoryTheory.Abelian D] →
            (k : Type t) →
              [inst_4 : Field k] →

                  [CategoryTheory.Linear k D] →
                    [CategoryTheory.HasExt C] → [CategoryTheory.HasExt D] → (C ≌ C) → C → C → D → D → Prop
docstring:
The bigraded `Ext` groups of `(X, Y)` **assemble into the ungraded `Ext` groups** of a pair
`(X', Y')`: in every cohomological degree the direct sum over the internal degrees of
`Ext^n(X, Y{j})` is `Ext^n(X', Y')`.

This is the hypothesis under which a q-Euler form specializes at `q = 1` to an ordinary Ext-Euler
characteristic.  A functor forgetting the grading supplies the intended pairs `(U X, U Y)`; the
existence of such a functor, or even of a shift-compatible one, does not by itself supply these
isomorphisms.
description:
**Graded Ext Comparison.** A pair of objects $(X, Y)$ in a graded abelian category $C$ and a pair of objects $(X', Y')$ in an abelian category $D$ satisfy the graded Ext comparison property if, for every cohomological degree $n$, there is a natural isomorphism between the $n$-th Ext group in $D$ and the direct sum over all internal shifts $j$ of the $n$-th bigraded Ext groups in $C$:
$$\text{Ext}^n_D(X', Y') \cong \bigoplus_{j \in \mathbb{Z}} \text{Ext}^n_C(X, Y\{j\}).$$

name: TauCeti.IsGlHighestWeightVector

A vector `v` of a `gl n R`-module is a **highest weight vector of weight `μ`** for the matrix
unit positive system when it is nonzero, the diagonal matrix unit `Eᵢᵢ` acts on it by the scalar
`μ i`, and every raising matrix unit `Eᵢⱼ` with `i < j` annihilates it.

The two elementwise families are coordinates for the diagonal Cartan subalgebra and generators of
the positive nilpotent subalgebra `𝔫⁺` — the nilpotent ideal of the standard Borel subalgebra
`TauCeti.upperTriangular R n`, not an ideal of `gl n R` — so this says exactly that `v` is a
`𝔫⁺`-annihilated weight
vector of weight `TauCeti.glWeightEquiv R n μ`; see
`TauCeti.isGlHighestWeightVector_iff_forall_mem`.
description: **Highest weight vector of the general linear Lie algebra.** Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ be a module over the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{gl}_n(R)$ of $n \times n$ matrices. A vector $v \in M$ is a highest weight vector of weight $\mu: n \to R$ (with respect to the standard Borel subalgebra) if $v$ is non-zero, each diagonal matrix unit $E_{ii}$ acts on $v$ by the scalar $\mu(i)$, and every strictly upper-triangular matrix unit $E_{ij}$ (where $i < j$) annihilates $v$.

Specifically, $\llbracket A, B \rrbracket = (A_{0,1}B_{1,2} - B_{0,1}A_{1,2}) \cdot Z$.

A normalized family of root vectors compatible with a Chevalley involution. The Lie
automorphism `ω` exchanges each root vector with the negative of its opposite.

There is no separate involutivity field: `TauCeti.IsChevalleySystem.involutive` proves it from this
compatibility and the fact that the root vectors and Cartan subalgebra span the ambient Lie

description: **Chevalley System.** A Chevalley system for a semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ with a fixed Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak{h}$ is a family of root vectors $\{x_\alpha\}_{\alpha \in \Phi}$ and a Lie algebra automorphism $\omega$ such that $\omega$ maps each root vector $x_\alpha$ to the negative of its corresponding opposite root vector $-x_{-\alpha}$. This compatibility, combined with the fact that the root vectors and the Cartan subalgebra span $\mathfrak{g}$, implies that $\omega$ is a Chevalley involution.

name: ContinuousLinearMap.exists_localStableSetHomeomorph
signature:
theorem ContinuousLinearMap.exists_localStableSetHomeomorph : ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup X] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ X] [CompleteSpace X] {K α ε : NNReal}
  (A P : X →L[ℝ] X) (N : X → X) (r : ℝ),
  (∀ (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → ∀ (v : X), ‖(NormedSpace.exp (t • A)) (P v)‖ ≤ ↑K * Real.exp (-↑α * t) * ‖v‖) →
    (∀ t ≤ 0, ∀ (v : X), ‖(NormedSpace.exp (t • A)) (v - P v)‖ ≤ ↑K * Real.exp (↑α * t) * ‖v‖) →
      LipschitzOnWith ε N (Metric.closedBall 0 r) →
        2 * K * (ε * 2) < α →
          N 0 = 0 →
            IsIdempotentElem P →
              Commute A P →
                0 < r →
                  ∃ ρ > 0,
                    Nonempty
                      (↑{v | ‖↑v‖ ≤ ρ} ≃ₜ
                        ↑{z |
                            (∃ y,
                                IsIntegralCurveOn y (fun x w => A w + N w) (Set.Ici 0) ∧
                                  y 0 = z ∧ Set.MapsTo y (Set.Ici 0) (Metric.closedBall 0 r)) ∧
                              ‖P z‖ ≤ ρ})
docstring:
For a small enough truncation radius, the local stable set of confined forward solutions is
homeomorphic to a closed ball in the stable spectral subspace.
description: **Homeomorphism between the Stable Subspace and the Local Stable Set.** Let $A$ be a continuous linear operator on a Banach space $X$, and let $P$ be a continuous projection that commutes with $A$. Suppose that $P$ defines a hyperbolic splitting such that the flow $e^{tA}$ is contracted by $K e^{-\alpha t}$ on the range of $P$ for $t \ge 0$, and is contracted by $K e^{\alpha t}$ on the kernel of $P$ for $t \le 0$. Let $N$ be a nonlinearity such that $N(0) = 0$ and $N$ is Lipschitz continuous on a closed ball of radius $r > 0$ with a sufficiently small Lipschitz constant $\varepsilon$ satisfying $4K\varepsilon < \alpha$. Then there exists a radius $\rho > 0$ such that the set of initial conditions $z$ whose forward integral curves under the vector field $Aw + N(w)$ remain within the ball of radius $r$ for all $t \ge 0$, and which satisfy $\|Pz\| \le \rho$, is homeomorphic to the closed ball of radius $\rho$ in the stable subspace $\text{ran}(P)$.

name: ContinuousLinearMap.norm_localUnstableGraphMap_le
signature:
theorem ContinuousLinearMap.norm_localUnstableGraphMap_le : ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup X] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ X] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace X] {K α ε : NNReal}
  {A P : X →L[ℝ] X} {N : X → X} {r : ℝ}
  (hs : ∀ (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → ∀ (v : X), ‖(NormedSpace.exp (t • A)) (P v)‖ ≤ ↑K * Real.exp (-↑α * t) * ‖v‖)
  (hu : ∀ t ≤ 0, ∀ (v : X), ‖(NormedSpace.exp (t • A)) (v - P v)‖ ≤ ↑K * Real.exp (↑α * t) * ‖v‖) (hr : 0 ≤ r)
  (hN : LipschitzOnWith ε N (Metric.closedBall 0 r)) (hsmall : 2 * K * (ε * 2) < α),
  N 0 = 0 →
    ∀ (v : X),
      ‖A.localUnstableGraphMap P N r hs hu hr hN hsmall v‖ ≤
        ↑(2 * K * (ε * 2) / α * (K / (1 - 2 * K * (ε * 2) / α))) * ‖v‖

If the nonlinearity fixes the equilibrium, the local unstable set lies in a cone around
`range (1 - P)` whose opening tends to `0` with the Lipschitz constant of the nonlinearity. This
is the unstable counterpart of `ContinuousLinearMap.norm_localStableGraphMap_le`.
description: **Bound on the Lipschitz constant of the local unstable manifold map.** Consider a complete normed space $X$ and a continuous linear operator $A$ on $X$. Let $P$ be a projection such that the semigroup generated by $A$ is exponentially contracting on the range of $P$ for $t \ge 0$ (with constants $K$ and $\alpha$) and exponentially contracting on the range of $I - P$ for $t \le 0$. Given a nonlinearity $N$ that is Lipschitz continuous with constant $\epsilon$ on a closed ball of radius $r$ around the origin and satisfies $N(0) = 0$, if the product of the Lipschitz constant and the growth constants is sufficiently small ($4K\epsilon < \alpha$), then the map defining the local unstable manifold is Lipschitz continuous. Specifically, the norm of the local unstable graph map at a point $v$ is bounded by $\frac{2K(2\epsilon)}{\alpha} \cdot \frac{K}{1 - 2K(2\epsilon)/\alpha} \|v\|$.

name: TauCeti.IsHyperellipticFunctionField
signature: structure TauCeti.IsHyperellipticFunctionField : (k : Type u_3) → (F : Type u_4) → [inst : Field k] → [inst_1 : Field F] → [Algebra k F] → Prop
docstring:
A **hyperelliptic function field** (Stichtenoth, Definition 6.2.1, with separability of the
index-two subextension made part of the definition): genus at least two together with an element
`x` transcendental over `k` such that `F / k(x)` is separable of degree two.

Being an algebraic function field is *not* part of the predicate: the hypothesis
`TauCeti.IsFunctionField`, like the exactness of the constant field, is kept as a separate
hypothesis on the statements that need it, as everywhere in this development.

In characteristic two an index-two subextension can be purely inseparable, and such an `F` is
deliberately outside this model class; away from characteristic two the separability clause is
automatic, so there the predicate agrees with Stichtenoth's index-two definition.
description: **Hyperelliptic Function Field.** A field extension $F/k$ is a hyperelliptic function field if $F$ has genus at least two and there exists an element $x \in F$, transcendental over $k$, such that the extension $F/k(x)$ is a separable quadratic extension.

name: TauCeti.Place.ratFuncDegreeOneEquiv

docstring:
**The rational places of `k(x)` are `ℙ¹(k) = k ∪ {∞}`** (Stichtenoth, Corollary 1.2.3): a
place of `k(x)` has degree one exactly when it is the place at infinity or the place of a linear
polynomial `X - a`.
description: **Equivalence between the Projective Line and Degree One Places.** For a field $k$, there is a natural bijection between the set $k \cup \{\infty\}$ (represented by the type `Option k`) and the set of places of the rational function field $k(x)$ that have degree one. Under this correspondence, an element $a \in k$ maps to the place associated with the linear polynomial $x - a$, while the element $\infty$ maps to the place at infinity.

name: TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.dualTensorHom_mem_internalHom_piece

description: **Degree of Rank-One Maps in Internal Hom Hodge Structures.** Given two complex vector spaces $W_1$ and $W_2$ equipped with Hodge structures of weights $n_1$ and $n_2$ respectively, let $\phi$ be a linear functional in the $p$-th piece of the dual Hodge structure on $W_1$, and let $y$ be an element in the $q$-th piece of the Hodge structure on $W_2$. Then the rank-one linear map $W_1 \to W_2$ defined by $x \mapsto \phi(x)y$ belongs to the $(p+q)$-th piece of the internal Hom Hodge structure from $W_1$ to $W_2$.

`u n → a`, the sequence is eventually above `a`, and `γ (u n) → y`, then `γ` extends before `a`.

Suppose $\gamma: \mathbb{R} \to M$ is an integral curve of $v$ on the open interval $(a, b)$ with $a < b$. If there exists a sequence $u_n$ in $(a, b)$ such that $u_n \to a$ and $\gamma(u_n)$ converges to some point $y \in M$, then there exists some $c < a$ and an integral curve $\delta$ defined on $(c, b)$ that agrees with $\gamma$ on the original interval $(a, b)$.

theorem TauCeti.SmoothEmbedding.Concordance.trans_apply_of_lt : ∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {E' : Type u_2}
  [inst_2 : NormedAddCommGroup E'] [inst_3 : NormedSpace ℝ E'] {H : Type u_3} [inst_4 : TopologicalSpace H]

  {M : Type u_5} [inst_6 : TopologicalSpace M] [inst_7 : ChartedSpace H M] {N : Type u_6} [inst_8 : TopologicalSpace N]
  [inst_9 : ChartedSpace H' N] {n : WithTop ℕ∞} {f g h : TauCeti.SmoothEmbedding I J n M N} [inst_10 : IsManifold I n M]
  [inst_11 : IsManifold J n N] [inst_12 : FiniteDimensional ℝ E'] (F : f.Concordance g) (G : g.Concordance h) (x : M)

description: **Transitivity of Concordances for $t > 1/2$.** Given two smooth concordances $F$ from $f$ to $g$ and $G$ from $g$ to $h$ between manifolds, the composition (transitivity) $(F \cdot G)$ evaluated at a point $x$ and time $t > 1/2$ is determined by the second concordance $G$.   {cov : CovariantDerivative I E fun x => TangentSpace I x} {Y Z : (x : M) → TangentSpace I x} {x : M},
  CovariantDerivative.IsLeviCivitaConnection I cov →
    ∀ (X : (x : M) → TangentSpace I x),
      (MDiffAt fun x => ⟨x, Y x⟩) x →
        (MDiffAt fun x => ⟨x, Z x⟩) x →
          ((d% fun y => inner ℝ (Y y) (Z y)) x) (X x) =
            inner ℝ ((↑cov Y x) (X x)) (Z x) + inner ℝ (Y x) ((↑cov Z x) (X x))
docstring:
Metric compatibility of a Levi-Civita connection, in the usable form
`X ⟪Y, Z⟫ = ⟪∇_X Y, Z⟫ + ⟪Y, ∇_X Z⟫`: this is
`CovariantDerivative.IsMetricCompatible.mvfderiv_inner_eq` read off the defining property
`IsLeviCivitaConnection.isMetricCompatible`.
description:
**Metric Compatibility of the Levi-Civita Connection.** For a Levi-Civita connection $
abla$ on a Riemannian manifold $M$, the directional derivative of the inner product of two vector fields $Y$ and $Z$ along a vector field $X$ satisfies the Leibniz rule:
$$X \langle Y, Z angle = \langle 
abla_X Y, Z angle + \langle Y, 
abla_X Z angle.$$
Specifically, if $Y$ and $Z$ are differentiable at a point $x \in M$, then the differential of the function $y \mapsto \langle Y(y), Z(y) angle$ at $x$ applied to the vector $X(x)$ is equal to the sum of the inner products $\langle (
abla Y)_x(X(x)), Z(x) angle$ and $\langle Y(x), (
abla Z)_x(X(x)) angle$.

The inclusion of the chart of a face factors through the face morphism into the chart of the
ambient cone.
description: **Factorization of Face Inclusion Maps in Toric Charts.** For a regular fan $\Phi$ and a face $\tau$ of a cone $\sigma$ in $\Phi$, the inclusion of the affine toric chart associated with $\tau$ into a scheme $Z$ factors through the morphism from the affine toric scheme of $\tau$ to that of $\sigma$, followed by the inclusion of the chart of $\sigma$ into $Z$. After the standard coordinate change, every unipotent Suzuki generator preserves the

The converse orientation of `TauCeti.instSMulCommClassPermutationAut`: the permutation

name: TauCeti.parityExtend_none

description: **Parity Extension at the None Element.** For any finite index set $\iota$ and any ring $F$, the parity extension of a function $x: \iota \to F$ evaluated at the element `none` is equal to the negative sum of all values of $x$ over $\iota$.

name: Set.weightEnumerator_eq_sum_monomial

theorem Set.weightEnumerator_eq_sum_monomial : ∀ {ι : Type u_1} {β : ι → Type u_2} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : (i : ι) → Zero (β i)]

    ∑ w ∈ Finset.range (Fintype.card ι + 1),
      (MvPolynomial.monomial ((fun₀ | 0 => Fintype.card ι - w) + fun₀ | 1 => w)) ↑(C.weightDistribution w)
docstring: The monomial form of the weight enumerator.
description: **Monomial form of the weight enumerator.** For a set of vectors $C \subseteq \prod_{i \in \iota} \beta_i$ over a finite index set $\iota$, the weight enumerator of $C$ is equal to the sum over all possible weights $w \in \{0, \dots, |\iota|\}$ of the monomials $X^{|\iota|-w} Y^w$ scaled by the weight distribution $A_w$, where $A_w$ is the number of elements in $C$ with Hamming weight $w$.

name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.isRowCommutation_comm

description: **Subdiagonal Successor Property.** For any non-zero natural number $n$ and any column index $c$ in the finite set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, applying the subdiagonal permutation of the grid to $c$ and incrementing the result by one yields the original index $c$.

name: TauCeti.GridRectangleDecomposition.IsRecutOfRightEqLeft
signature:
def TauCeti.GridRectangleDecomposition.IsRecutOfRightEqLeft : {n : ℕ} →
  {x z : TauCeti.GridState n} → TauCeti.GridRectangleDecomposition x z → TauCeti.GridRectangleDecomposition x z → Prop
docstring:
The side data of the recut of a decomposition whose common column is the terminal side of its
first rectangle and the initial side of its second.
description: **Recutting Condition for Adjacent Rectangles.** For a grid rectangle decomposition between two states, the property of being a "recut" holds when the common column shared by the rectangles in the decomposition is simultaneously the right (terminal) boundary of the first rectangle and the left (initial) boundary of the second rectangle.

name: TauCeti.GridRectangleDecomposition.IsRecutOfRightEqRight.recut_branch
signature:
theorem TauCeti.GridRectangleDecomposition.IsRecutOfRightEqRight.recut_branch : ∀ {n : ℕ} {x z : TauCeti.GridState n} {D E : TauCeti.GridRectangleDecomposition x z},
  D.IsRecutOfRightEqRight E →
    D.first.left ∈ TauCeti.Grid.cIoo D.second.left D.first.right ∧
        E.middle = TauCeti.GridState.swapColumns D.second.left D.first.left x ∧
          E.first.right = D.first.left ∧ E.second.right = D.first.right ∨
      D.second.left ∈ TauCeti.Grid.cIoo D.first.left D.first.right ∧
        E.middle = TauCeti.GridState.swapColumns D.second.left D.first.right x ∧
          E.first.right = D.first.right ∧ E.second.right = D.second.left
docstring: The column and branch data of a `right = right` recut.
description:
**Column and Branch Data for a Right-Equal-Right Recut.** For any grid rectangle decompositions $D$ and $E$ where $E$ is a "right = right" recut of $D$, the configuration of the columns and the middle state of $E$ must satisfy one of two cases:

1. The left boundary of $D$'s first rectangle lies strictly between the left boundary of $D$'s second rectangle and the shared right boundary of $D$'s first rectangle. In this case, the middle state of $E$ is obtained by swapping the columns at the left boundaries of $D$'s second and first rectangles, while the right boundaries of $E$'s first and second rectangles are given by the left and right boundaries of $D$'s first rectangle, respectively.

2. The left boundary of $D$'s second rectangle lies strictly between the left and right boundaries of $D$'s first rectangle. In this case, the middle state of $E$ is obtained by swapping the columns at the left boundary of $D$'s second rectangle and the right boundary of $D$'s first rectangle, while the right boundaries of $E$'s first and second rectangles are given by the right boundary of $D$'s first rectangle and the left boundary of $D$'s second rectangle, respectively.

name: TauCeti.GridRectangle.mem_coveredSquares_swap_iff_of_coveredColumns
signature:
theorem TauCeti.GridRectangle.mem_coveredSquares_swap_iff_of_coveredColumns : ∀ {n : ℕ} (R : TauCeti.GridRectangle n) {a b : Fin n},
  (a ∈ R.coveredColumns ↔ b ∈ R.coveredColumns) →
    ∀ (p : Fin n × Fin n), ((Equiv.swap a b) p.1, p.2) ∈ R.coveredSquares ↔ p ∈ R.coveredSquares
docstring:
Swapping two columns preserves a rectangle's covered squares when the rectangle either
covers both columns or covers neither.
description: **Invariance of Covered Squares under Column Swapping.** For a grid rectangle $R$ of size $n \times n$ and any two column indices $a$ and $b$, if $a$ and $b$ are either both covered by $R$ or both not covered by $R$, then a point $(x, y)$ is a covered square of $R$ if and only if the point resulting from swapping the column indices $a$ and $b$ is also a covered square of $R$.

name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.twoByTwo_X

name: TauCeti.FramedMarkovBraid
signature: structure TauCeti.FramedMarkovBraid : Type
docstring:
A framed oriented braid-closure presentation. The braid direction supplies the orientation.
A framing of an oriented link in `S³`, relative to the Seifert framing, is specified by one
integer coefficient on each component; the components of a braid closure are the orbits of its
underlying permutation. The projection `forgetFraming` drops this data to the ordinary unframed
braid on which `TauCeti.MarkovEquiv` is defined.
description: **Framed Oriented Braid-Closure.** A framed oriented braid-closure is a mathematical structure representing an oriented link in $S^3$ equipped with a framing. The orientation of the link is induced by the braid direction, and the framing is defined relative to the Seifert framing by assigning an integer coefficient to each connected component of the link. These components correspond to the orbits of the permutation underlying the braid. The structure includes a projection that recovers the underlying unframed braid by forgetting the integer framing coefficients.

name: Module.Basis.coord_map_apply
signature:
theorem Module.Basis.coord_map_apply : ∀ {R : Type u_4} {M : Type u_5} {M' : Type u_6} {ι : Type u_7} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M]
  [inst_2 : Module R M] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid M'] [inst_4 : Module R M'] (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (f : M ≃ₗ[R] M')
  (i : ι) (x : M'), ((b.map f).coord i) x = (b.coord i) (f.symm x)
docstring:
The coordinates with respect to the basis `b.map f` transported along a linear equivalence
`f` are the coordinates with respect to `b` of the vector transported back along `f`. Not a simp
lemma: simp already unfolds the left side through `Module.Basis.coord_apply`.
description: **Coordinate Map of a Transported Basis.** Given a basis $b = \{e_i\}_{i \in I}$ for a module $M$ over a semiring $R$ and a linear equivalence $f: M \cong M'$, the $i$-th coordinate of a vector $x \in M'$ with respect to the transported basis $f(b)$ is equal to the $i$-th coordinate of $f^{-1}(x)$ with respect to the original basis $b$.

name: TauCeti.torusCharacter_sub

theorem TauCeti.torusCharacter_sub : ∀ {κ : Type v} {R : Type w} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Fintype κ] (s : κ → Rˣ) (μ ν : κ → ℤ),
  TauCeti.torusCharacter s (μ - ν) = TauCeti.torusCharacter s μ / TauCeti.torusCharacter s ν
docstring: Subtracting weights divides the values of their characters.
description:
**Torus Character of a Difference of Weights.** For any finite index set $\kappa$ and commutative ring $R$, let $s: \kappa 	o R^	imes$ be a collection of units and $\mu, 
u: \kappa 	o \mathbb{Z}$ be weights. The character of the torus evaluated at the difference of the weights $\mu - 
u$ is equal to the quotient of the character evaluated at $\mu$ and the character evaluated at $
u$.

name: TauCeti.realCliffordBottEquiv_ι
signature:
theorem TauCeti.realCliffordBottEquiv_ι : ∀ (p q : ℕ) (v : Fin (p + 1 + (q + 1)) → ℝ),
  (TauCeti.realCliffordBottEquiv p q) ((CliffordAlgebra.ι (TauCeti.realCliffordForm (p + 1) (q + 1))) v) =
    (CliffordAlgebra.ι (TauCeti.realCliffordForm p q)) ((TauCeti.realBottSplitIsometry p q) v).1 ⊗ₜ[ℝ] !![0, 1; 1, 0] +
      1 ⊗ₜ[ℝ]
        !![((TauCeti.realBottSplitIsometry p q) v).2 0, ((TauCeti.realBottSplitIsometry p q) v).2 1;
          -((TauCeti.realBottSplitIsometry p q) v).2 1, -((TauCeti.realBottSplitIsometry p q) v).2 0]
docstring:
`realCliffordBottEquiv` first separates the last positive and negative coordinates, then
applies the hyperbolic-plane equivalence.
description: **Action of the Real Clifford-Bott Equivalence on Generators.** The isomorphism between the Clifford algebras $C\ell_{p+1, q+1}(\mathbb{R})$ and $C\ell_{p, q}(\mathbb{R}) \otimes \text{Mat}_2(\mathbb{R})$ maps a vector $v$ in the generating space of $C\ell_{p+1, q+1}(\mathbb{R})$ to a sum of two tensors. Specifically, it maps the inclusion of $v$ to the tensor product of the inclusion of the first component of the isometry $\text{realBottSplitIsometry}(v)$ in $C\ell_{p, q}(\mathbb{R})$ with the matrix $\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}$, plus the tensor product of the identity in $C\ell_{p, q}(\mathbb{R})$ with the matrix $\begin{pmatrix} v'_0 & v'_1 \\ -v'_1 & -v'_0 \end{pmatrix}$, where $(v'_0, v'_1)$ are the coordinates of the second component of the isometry.

name: TauCeti.realCliffordZeroOneIsometry_apply

docstring: `realCliffordZeroOneIsometry` reads off the single coordinate.
description: **Evaluation of the Real Clifford Isometry.** The isometry $\text{realCliffordZeroOneIsometry}$ maps a vector $v$ in the one-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^1$ (indexed by $\text{Fin}(1)$) to its single coordinate $v_0$.

name: QuadraticMap.IsometryEquiv.spinGroupEquiv_apply
docstring: The equivalence induced on Spin groups agrees with the forward isometry map.
description: **Action of Spin Group Equivalences.** For an isometry equivalence $e$ between two quadratic forms $Q_1$ and $Q_2$ over a commutative ring, the induced isomorphism between their respective Spin groups $Spin(Q_1)$ and $Spin(Q_2)$ maps an element $x$ in the same way as the homomorphism induced by the underlying isometry of $e$.

docstring: The quotient map sends an element to its quotient class.
description: **Quotient Map Evaluation.** For a finite bilinear module $A$ and a subgroup $K$ of its radical, the quotient map induced by $K$ maps any element $x \in A$ to its corresponding coset in the quotient module $A/K$.

name: TauCeti.FiniteQuadraticModule.zmodStandard_quadratic

description: **Quadratic Map of the Standard Quadratic Module over $\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$.** For any positive even integer $m$, the quadratic map associated with the standard quadratic module on $\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z}$ is given by the mapping $x \mapsto \frac{x^2}{2m} \pmod 1$.

name: TauCeti.IntegralLattice.orthogonalSumFst_apply
signature:
theorem TauCeti.IntegralLattice.orthogonalSumFst_apply : ∀ {V : Type u} {W : Type v} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : Module ℚ V] [inst_2 : AddCommGroup W]

name: TauCeti.IntegralLattice.typeARootLattice
signature: def TauCeti.IntegralLattice.typeARootLattice : (n : ℕ) → TauCeti.IntegralLattice (Fin n → ℚ)
docstring:
The positive root lattice of type `Aₙ`: the rank-`n` integral lattice on `Fin n → ℚ` whose
Gram matrix in the standard basis of simple roots is `CartanMatrix.A n`.
description: **The Type $A_n$ Root Lattice.** For any natural number $n$, the root lattice of type $A_n$ is the rank-$n$ integral lattice defined on the vector space $\mathbb{Q}^n$ such that the Gram matrix relative to the standard basis of simple roots is the Cartan matrix of type $A_n$.

name: TauCeti.IntegralLattice.isPosSemidef_iff

theorem TauCeti.IntegralLattice.isPosSemidef_iff : ∀ {V : Type u} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : Module ℚ V] (L : TauCeti.IntegralLattice V),

docstring: Positive-semidefiniteness has its usual elementwise characterization.
description: **Characterization of Positive-Semidefiniteness for Integral Lattices.** For an integral lattice $L$ on a $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space $V$, the lattice is positive-semidefinite if and only if its associated bilinear form is non-negative for all vectors in $V$; that is, $L.form(x, x) \ge 0$ for every $x \in V$.

name: TauCeti.GL2Borel.quotientEquivOnePoint_symm_infty

theorem TauCeti.GL2Borel.quotientEquivOnePoint_symm_infty : ∀ (F : Type u) [inst : Field F] [inst_1 : DecidableEq F],

docstring: The coset carried to `∞` is the Borel subgroup itself.
description: **The Inverse Image of Infinity under the GL₂(F)/Borel Correspondence.** For any field $F$, the inverse of the bijection between the quotient of $GL_2(F)$ by its Borel subgroup and the projective line $\mathbb{P}^1(F)$ maps the point at infinity $\infty$ to the identity coset of the Borel subgroup.

name: TauCeti.GLSymplecticFin.RootSubgroupIndex
signature: inductive TauCeti.GLSymplecticFin.RootSubgroupIndex : ℕ → Type
docstring:
An extensional index for the root one-parameter subgroups of the standard symplectic group.

Difference roots retain their ordered pair of indices. The symmetric positive- and negative-sum
roots store their indices in increasing order, so each root has only one index.
description: **Symplectic Root Subgroup Index.** The type of indices for the root one-parameter subgroups of the standard symplectic group of rank $n$. This indexing set consists of three types of roots: difference roots, represented as ordered pairs of distinct indices $(i, j)$; and symmetric positive-sum and negative-sum roots, each represented by a pair of indices $(i, j)$ with $i \le j$ to ensure a unique representation for each root.

name: Matrix.pairMinor_transpose

theorem Matrix.pairMinor_transpose : ∀ {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {R : Type u} [inst : CommRing R] (g : Matrix m n R) (p : m × m) (q : n × n),

A minor of the transpose is the minor of the matrix with the row and column pairs
exchanged.
description: **Transpose of a Pair Minor.** For any matrix $g$ over a commutative ring, the minor formed by a pair of indices $q$ and $p$ from its transpose is equal to the minor formed by the pairs $p$ and $q$ from the original matrix $g$.

name: TauCeti.SL2Borel.coe_mk

name: TauCeti.mem_closure_image_piAlgebraMap

Entrywise base change carries the additive closure of a family into the additive closure of the

For any family of elements $g_i \in R^\kappa$ indexed by $i \in \iota$ and any subset $s \subseteq \iota$, if an element $x \in R^\kappa$ belongs to the additive submonoid generated by $\{g_i \mid i \in s\}$, then its image under the entrywise algebra map $\pi: R^\kappa \to S^\kappa$ belongs to the additive submonoid generated by the images $\{\pi(g_i) \mid i \in s\}$.

name: TauCeti.mem_weylChamber

name: TauCeti.HeegaardIntersectionSystem
signature: structure TauCeti.HeegaardIntersectionSystem : ℕ → Type u → Type u
docstring:
Finite intersection data for two equally sized curve systems. The finite enumeration records
the point set, and each point has one `α`-curve label and one `β`-curve label; geometric surface
and region data are additional structure.
description: **Heegaard Intersection System.** A Heegaard intersection system is a structure representing the finite intersection data between two systems of curves, denoted $\alpha$ and $\beta$, of equal size $n$. The system consists of a finite set of intersection points, where each point is uniquely associated with one curve from the $\alpha$-system and one curve from the $\beta$-system. This structure serves as a foundation for additional geometric data concerning the underlying surface and its regions.

name: TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.IsNegativeDefinite.intersectionForm_nondegenerate

docstring:
The intersection form of a negative-definite plumbing is nondegenerate: a lattice vector that
pairs to zero with every vector — in particular with itself — is zero, on either side.
description: **Nondegeneracy of the Intersection Form for Negative-Definite Plumbing Graphs.** For any plumbing graph whose intersection form is negative-definite, the intersection form is nondegenerate. That is, if a vector in the associated lattice pairs to zero with every other vector, it must be the zero vector.

description: **Equality of characteristic weights under blow-up.** For a plumbing graph $P$ and its blow-up at a vertex $v$ with exceptional weight $\varepsilon$, the characteristic weight of the blown-up characteristic vector at a point $(x, s)$ in the blown-up lattice is equal to the characteristic weight of the original vector at $x$ if and only if the multiplicity $s$ of the exceptional divisor is either $0$ or $\varepsilon$.

theorem TauCeti.enorm_setAverage_rpow_le : ∀ {α : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {mu : MeasureTheory.Measure α}
  [inst_1 : NormedAddCommGroup F] [inst_2 : NormedSpace ℝ F] {f : α → F} {s : Set α} {q : ℝ},
  1 ≤ q →
    MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable f mu →
      mu s ≠ 0 → mu s ≠ ⊤ → ‖⨍ (y : α) in s, f y ∂mu‖ₑ ^ q ≤ (mu s)⁻¹ * ∫⁻ (y : α) in s, ‖f y‖ₑ ^ q ∂mu

**Hölder's bound on an average**, in `∫⁻` form: the `q`-th power of the average of `f` over a
set `s` of finite positive measure is at most `(μ s)⁻¹` times the integral of `‖f‖ ^ q` over `s`.

`(μ s)⁻¹` cancels against the `(μ s) ^ (q - 1)` of Hölder's inequality.
description: **Hölder's Inequality for Averaged Integrals.** For a real number $q \geq 1$, a measurable set $s$ with finite positive measure $\mu(s)$, and an almost everywhere strongly measurable function $f$, the $q$-th power of the norm of the average value of $f$ over $s$ is bounded by the average of the $q$-th power of the norm of $f$. **Boundary data for the prime Dirichlet series of `S`.**  The function `series` is the sum
of the Dirichlet series of `primeVonMangoldtCoeff K S` on `Re s > 1`.  The function `remainder`
is continuous on `Re s ≥ 1` and agrees on the open half-plane with
`series s - δ / (s - 1)`.

arbitrary values elsewhere.
description: **Boundary Data for the Prime Dirichlet Series.** For a number field $K$, a set of prime ideals $S$ in its ring of integers, and a real density $\delta$, this structure represents the analytic boundary data for the Dirichlet series associated with the prime-weighted von Mangoldt coefficients of $S$. name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_cmRadicand

theorem TauCeti.Multiquadratic.not_isSquare_prod_cmRadicand : ∀ {ι : Type u_1} (p : ι → ℕ),

docstring:
The CM radicand family is square-class independent: for distinct primes `p`, no nonempty
subset product of `-1, p₁, …, pₙ` is a square in `ℚ`.
description: **Square-Class Independence of the CM Radicand Family.** Let $p: \iota \to \mathbb{N}$ be an injective sequence of prime numbers. For any $i \in \iota$, let the radicands be defined by the family $\{-1\} \cup \{p_i\}_{i \in \iota}$. Then, the product of any non-empty finite subset of these radicands is never a square in $\mathbb{Q}$.

name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.ramificationIdx_eq_two_of_liesOver_primeDiscriminantPrime
signature:
theorem TauCeti.Multiquadratic.ramificationIdx_eq_two_of_liesOver_primeDiscriminantPrime : ∀ {ι : Type u} [Finite ι] {L : Type v} [inst : Field L] [inst_1 : NumberField L] (D : ι → ℤ) (root : ι → L),
  (∀ (i : ι), TauCeti.Multiquadratic.IsPrimeDiscriminant (D i)) →
    Function.Injective D →
      (∀ (i j : ι),
          TauCeti.Multiquadratic.IsEvenPrimeDiscriminant (D i) →
            TauCeti.Multiquadratic.IsEvenPrimeDiscriminant (D j) → D i = D j) →
        (∀ (i : ι), root i ^ 2 = (algebraMap ℚ L) ↑(TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantRadicand (D i))) →
          IntermediateField.adjoin ℚ (Set.range root) = ⊤ →
            ∀ (i : ι) (𝔓 : Ideal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers L)) [𝔓.IsPrime]
              [𝔓.LiesOver (Ideal.span {↑(TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantPrime (D i))})],
              𝔓.ramificationIdx ℤ = 2
docstring:
**The ramification index at a ramified prime of a prime-discriminant compositum is `2`.**
However many factors the compositum has, a prime belonging to one of them has ramification index
exactly two: the inertia subgroup at a ramified prime is as small as it can be.

The upper bound is transverse cancellation. The compositum `U` of the other roots is unramified at
the prime (`isUnramifiedIn_adjoin_range_ne_primeDiscriminantPrime`), so the absolute ramification
index equals the relative one over `U`, which is at most `[L : U] = 2`. The lower bound is the
total ramification of the quadratic subfield `ℚ(root i)`.
description: **Ramification Index of a Prime-Discriminant Compositum.** Let $L$ be a number field formed by the compositum of quadratic extensions $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d_i})$ for a finite set of distinct prime discriminants $d_i$. Specifically, assume $L = \mathbb{Q}(\{\sqrt{d_i^*}\}_{i \in \iota})$ where each $d_i$ is a prime discriminant, the map $i \mapsto d_i$ is injective, at most one $d_i$ is even, and $d_i^*$ denotes the radicand associated with the discriminant $d_i$. For any index $i$, let $p_i$ be the unique prime number dividing the discriminant $d_i$. If $\mathfrak{P}$ is a prime ideal of the ring of integers of $L$ lying over the principal ideal $(p_i)$ in $\mathbb{Z}$, then the absolute ramification index of $\mathfrak{P}$ over $\mathbb{Z}$ is exactly $2$.

theorem TauCeti.Multiquadratic.intermediateFieldEquivSubmoduleSqrtPrimes_apply_ofDual_eq : ∀ {ι : Type u_1} [inst : Finite ι] (p : ι → ℕ) (hp : ∀ (i : ι), Nat.Prime (p i)) (hinj : Function.Injective p)

The subspace attached by the public prime-radicand dictionary is extensionally the same as
the generic dictionary fed the prime-family square-class independence proof. This lets consumers
use the degree theorems from `SubfieldDegree` with
`intermediateFieldEquivSubmoduleSqrtPrimes` without a parallel prime-specific degree API.
description: **Equivalence of Submodule Mappings for Multiquadratic Fields.** For a finite family of distinct prime numbers $(p_i)_{i \in \iota}$, the isomorphism that maps intermediate fields of the multiquadratic extension $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{p_i} : i \in \iota)$ to submodules of the square-class group is extensionally equivalent to the generic dictionary mapping intermediate fields to submodules when specialized to the square roots of these primes. Consequently, the submodule associated with an intermediate field $F$ via the prime-specific radicand mapping is identical to the submodule associated with $F$ via the general square-class independence construction.

name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.IsNarrowGenusField
signature: structure TauCeti.Multiquadratic.IsNarrowGenusField : ℤ → (L : Type u) → [inst : Field L] → [NumberField L] → L → Prop
docstring:
An abelian extension `L / ℚ`, with a chosen quadratic subfield generated by `y² = d`, is a
**narrow genus field** when it is unramified over that subfield at every finite place and is
maximal among abelian extensions with those properties.

No condition is imposed at infinite places. This is the distinction between the narrow genus
field and the everywhere-unramified genus field for a real quadratic radicand.
description: **Narrow Genus Field.** Let $L$ be an abelian extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ and let $d \in \mathbb{Z}$ be a square-free integer such that $L$ contains the quadratic subfield $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d})$. We say that $L$ is the narrow genus field of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d})$ if $L$ is unramified at all finite places over $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d})$ and is maximal among all abelian extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$ satisfying this property. Unlike the standard genus field, no condition is imposed on the ramification of the infinite places.

name: TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.ideleCongruenceSubgroup

docstring:
**The idele congruence subgroup of a modulus**: the ideles congruent to one modulo `𝔪` that
are moreover units of the valuation ring at the finite places not dividing `𝔪`.  Explicitly, they
are principal units of the prescribed level at the finite divisors of `𝔪`, units of the valuation
ring at the remaining finite places, and positive at the real places selected by `𝔪`.  No
condition is imposed at the infinite places outside `𝔪`.
description: **Idele Congruence Subgroup.** For a global number field $K$ and a modulus $\mathfrak{m}$, the idele congruence subgroup is the subgroup of the idele group of $K$ consisting of ideles $x = (x_v)_v$ such that: at each finite place $v$ dividing the finite part of $\mathfrak{m}$, $x_v$ is a principal unit of level $v(\mathfrak{m})$; at each finite place $v$ not dividing $\mathfrak{m}$, $x_v$ is a unit in the local ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_v$; and at each real place $v$ dividing the infinite part of $\mathfrak{m}$, $x_v$ is strictly positive. No conditions are imposed at infinite places not contained in the support of $\mathfrak{m}$.

signature:
theorem TauCeti.NumberFieldArithmetic.artinElementAway_eq_of_isArithFrobAt : ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] {L : Type u_2} [inst_2 : Field L] [inst_3 : NumberField L]
  [inst_4 : Algebra K L] [inst_5 : IsGalois K L] (hab : ∀ (σ τ : Gal(L/K)), Commute σ τ)
  (S : Finset (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)))
  (hur :
    ∀ v ∉ S,
      ∀ (Q : Ideal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers L)) [inst_6 : Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver v.asIdeal],
        Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) Q)
  {v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)},
  v ∉ S →
    ∀ (Q : Ideal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers L)) [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver v.asIdeal] {σ : Gal(L/K)},
      IsArithFrobAt (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) σ Q → TauCeti.NumberFieldArithmetic.artinElementAway hab S hur v = σ
docstring:
**The Artin automorphism at `v ∉ S` is the Frobenius there.** Any arithmetic Frobenius at any
prime above `v` equals it, which is what makes the assignment `v ↦ artinElementAway hab S hur v`
well defined without a choice of prime above `v`.
description: **Equality of the Artin Map and the Arithmetic Frobenius.** Let $L/K$ be a Galois extension of number fields with an abelian Galois group $\text{Gal}(L/K)$. Let $S$ be a finite set of prime ideals of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ containing all primes that ramify in $L$. For any prime $v$ of $\mathcal{O}_K$ not in $S$, the Artin element at $v$ is equal to any automorphism $\sigma \in \text{Gal}(L/K)$ that acts as an arithmetic Frobenius at a prime ideal $Q$ of $\mathcal{O}_L$ lying over $v$.

name: TauCeti.rationalPrimeBelow
signature: def TauCeti.rationalPrimeBelow : {K : Type u_1} → [inst : Field K] → IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) → ℕ
docstring:
The rational prime below a height-one prime `𝔭` of `𝓞 K`, that is, the residue
characteristic of `𝔭`.  It is the absolute norm of the prime `𝔭 ∩ ℤ` of `ℤ`.
description: **Rational Prime Below a Height-One Prime.** For a number field $K$, the rational prime below a height-one prime ideal $\mathfrak{p}$ of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ is the unique prime number $p \in \mathbb{N}$ that generates the ideal $\mathfrak{p} \cap \mathbb{Z}$. This value corresponds to the residue characteristic of $\mathfrak{p}$ and the absolute norm of the prime ideal $\mathfrak{p} \cap \mathbb{Z}$ in $\mathbb{Z}$.

name: IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.intCast_mem_asIdeal_iff
signature:
theorem IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.intCast_mem_asIdeal_iff : ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] (𝔭 : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)) (n : ℤ),
  ↑n ∈ 𝔭.asIdeal ↔ ↑(TauCeti.rationalPrimeBelow 𝔭) ∣ n
docstring:
An integer belongs to a height-one prime exactly when the rational prime below it divides that
integer.
description: **Membership of Integers in Height-One Prime Ideals.** For a number field $K$, let $\mathfrak{p}$ be a height-one prime ideal of its ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$. An integer $n$ belongs to $\mathfrak{p}$ if and only if the rational prime $p$ lying below $\mathfrak{p}$ divides $n$.

name: QuadraticForm.atRealPlaceWeightedSumSquares_apply
signature:
theorem QuadraticForm.atRealPlaceWeightedSumSquares_apply : ∀ {K : Type u} [inst : Field K] {ι : Type u_1} [inst_1 : Fintype ι] (w : { w // w.IsReal }) (a : ι → K)
  (x : TauCeti.RealScalarExtension w),
  let x_1 := (NumberField.InfinitePlace.embedding_of_isReal ⋯).toAlgebra;
  (QuadraticForm.atRealPlaceWeightedSumSquares w a) x = (TensorProduct.piScalarRightHom K ℝ ℝ ι) x
docstring:
The underlying linear map of the real-place diagonal isometry is the canonical distribution
of tensor product over the finite coordinate space.
description: **Evaluation of the Weighted Sum of Squares at a Real Place.** For a field $K$, a finite index set $\iota$, and a real infinite place $w$ of $K$, let $x$ be an element of the scalar extension of $K$ to $\mathbb{R}$ via the embedding associated with $w$. The quadratic form defined as the weighted sum of squares at $w$ with coefficients $a: \iota \to K$, when evaluated at $x$, is equal to the value of the canonical linear map that distributes the tensor product over the finite coordinate space $\mathbb{R}^\iota$ applied to $x$.

name: TauCeti.Probability.blockLaw_def

theorem TauCeti.Probability.blockLaw_def : ∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_4} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] [inst_1 : MeasurableSpace α]

description: **Definition of the Joint Distribution of a Sequence of Random Variables.** For a measure space $\Omega$, a measurable space $\alpha$, a measure $\mu$ on $\Omega$, and a collection of random variables $X_i: \Omega \to \alpha$ indexed by $i \in \iota$, the block law of a finite sequence of these variables indexed by $k: \{0, \dots, m-1\} \to \iota$ is defined as the pushforward measure of $\mu$ under the map $\omega \mapsto (X_{k(0)}(\omega), \dots, X_{k(m-1)}(\omega))$.

The numbered class-multiplication matrices commute pairwise, the centre of the group algebra

description: **Commutativity of Class-Multiplication Matrices.** For a finite group $G$, the class-multiplication matrices associated with its conjugacy classes commute pairwise. This reflects the fact that the center of the group algebra is a commutative algebra.

name: Rep.augmentation

The **augmentation** `k[G] ⟶ k`, the map of representations sending a group ring element to
the sum of its coefficients; it is the map out of the left regular representation attached to

description: **Augmentation map.** For a commutative ring $k$ and a group $G$, the augmentation is the morphism of $k$-linear representations from the left regular representation of $G$ to the trivial representation of $G$ on $k$ that maps each element of the group ring $k[G]$ to the sum of its coefficients.

description: **The degree-two component of the bar homotopy for inverse conjugation.** Given a group $K$ and a type $A$ equipped with a subtraction operation, this function defines the degree-two component of the bar homotopy associated with inverse conjugation. Specifically, it takes an element $k \in K$, a 2-cochain $f: K \times K \to A$, and another element of $K$ to produce an element in $A$.

name: TauCeti.continuousSMulQuotientFixedPointsOfContinuousSMul
signature:
instance TauCeti.continuousSMulQuotientFixedPointsOfContinuousSMul : ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G] [inst_1 : TopologicalSpace G] (M : Type u_2) [inst_2 : AddGroup M]
  [inst_3 : DistribMulAction G M] [inst_4 : TopologicalSpace M] [DiscreteTopology M] [ContinuousSMul G M]
  (H : Subgroup G) [inst_7 : H.Normal], ContinuousSMul (G ⧸ H) ↥(FixedPoints.addSubgroup (↥H) M)
docstring:
For an arbitrary normal subgroup `H`, the action of `G ⧸ H` on the invariants `M ^ H` of a
discrete module is continuous. Unlike
`TauCeti.continuousSMulQuotientFixedPoints`, which reads the continuity off the discreteness of
`G ⧸ H` for open `H` and needs no continuity of the `G`-action, this deduces it from continuity of
the `G`-action: the invariants are discrete, so continuity is continuity in the group variable
alone, and there it is the continuity of the `G`-action read through the quotient map. No
compatibility of the topology of `G` with its group structure is needed, since `G ⧸ H` carries the
quotient topology.
description: **Continuity of the Quotient Action on Invariants.** Let $G$ be a topological group and $M$ be a discrete topological additive group equipped with a continuous distributive action of $G$. For any normal subgroup $H$ of $G$, the induced action of the quotient group $G/H$ (endowed with the quotient topology) on the subgroup of $H$-invariant elements $M^H$ is continuous.

name: Rep.FiniteCyclicGroup.tateCohomologyIsoOdd_negOne

description: **Tate Cohomology Comparison in Degree -1.** For a representation $M$ of a finite cyclic group $G$ generated by $g$ over a commutative ring $R$, the isomorphism between Tate cohomology groups in odd degrees specializes in degree $-1$ to the standard isomorphism $H^{-1}(G, M) \cong \text{ker}(N)/\text{im}(\sigma - 1)$.

name: TauCeti.conjNormalFDRepEquiv
signature:
def TauCeti.conjNormalFDRepEquiv : {k : Type u} →
  {G : Type v} →
    [inst : Group G] → {N : Subgroup G} → [hN : N.Normal] → [inst_1 : Ring k] → G → (FDRep k ↥N ≌ FDRep k ↥N)
docstring:
Conjugation by `g` is an autoequivalence of `FDRep k N`, with inverse conjugation by `g⁻¹`:
Mathlib's `Action.resEquiv` for the automorphism `MulAut.conjNormal g⁻¹` of `N`.

The body is sealed, as for `conjNormalRepEquiv`; `conjNormalFDRepEquiv_functor` and
`conjNormalFDRepEquiv_inverse` are the interface identifying it with conjugation.
description: **Equivalence of Finite-Dimensional Representations induced by Normal Conjugation.** For a group $G$ with a normal subgroup $N$ and a ring $k$, any element $g \in G$ induces an autoequivalence of the category of finite-dimensional $k$-linear representations of $N$. This equivalence is given by the restriction of scalars along the conjugation automorphism $n \mapsto g^{-1}ng$ of $N$, with its inverse provided by conjugation by $g^{-1}$.

name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.indVirtualCharacters
signature:
def TauCeti.ClassFunction.indVirtualCharacters : (k : Type u) →
  (G : Type v) → [inst : Field k] → [inst_1 : Group G] → [Finite G] → (Subgroup G → Prop) → AddSubgroup (G → k)
docstring:
**The virtual characters of `G` induced from a family of subgroups**: the additive subgroup of
`G → k` generated by `Ind_S^G ψ` for `S` satisfying `P` and `ψ` a virtual character of `S`.

For `P` the cyclic or elementary subgroups this is the subgroup generated by induction from their
virtual-character lattices; it is the image of the induction map `⨁_S R(S) → R(G)`.
description: **Induction of Virtual Characters from a Family of Subgroups.** Given a finite group $G$, a field $k$, and a property $P$ of subgroups of $G$, this is the additive subgroup of the space of class functions $G \to k$ generated by the set of all virtual characters of $G$ induced from virtual characters of subgroups $S \le G$ that satisfy the property $P$.

name: Rep.coindBotUnit_mono

docstring: The embedding into the coinduced representation is a monomorphism.
description: **Monomorphism of the Coinduced Representation Embedding.** For any representation $A$ of a group $G$ over a commutative ring $k$, the natural embedding into the coinduced representation, denoted by $A.\text{coindBotUnit}$, is a monomorphism in the category of representations.

name: TauCeti.Representation.isIrreducible_of_linearEquiv
signature:
theorem TauCeti.Representation.isIrreducible_of_linearEquiv : ∀ {k : Type u_1} {G : Type u_2} {V : Type u_3} [inst : Field k] [inst_1 : Monoid G] [inst_2 : AddCommGroup V]
  [inst_3 : Module k V] {W : Type u_4} [inst_4 : AddCommGroup W] [inst_5 : Module k W] {ρ : Representation k G V}
  {σ : Representation k G W} (e : V ≃ₗ[k] W),
  (∀ (g : G) (v : V), e ((ρ g) v) = (σ g) (e v)) → ρ.IsIrreducible → σ.IsIrreducible
docstring:
**Irreducibility transports along an equivariant linear equivalence.** A linear equivalence
intertwining two representations matches their lattices of subrepresentations, by taking preimages
of invariant subspaces, so one is irreducible exactly when the other is.

Only one direction is stated; the reverse is this one applied to `e.symm`.
description: **Irreducibility of Representations under Equivariant Linear Equivalence.** Let $\rho$ and $\sigma$ be representations of a monoid $G$ over a field $k$ on the vector spaces $V$ and $W$, respectively. If there exists a $k$-linear equivalence $e: V \cong W$ that is equivariant with respect to the action of $G$—that is, $e(\rho(g)v) = \sigma(g)e(v)$ for all $g \in G$ and $v \in V$—then the irreducibility of $\rho$ implies the irreducibility of $\sigma$.

name: TauCeti.finiteDimensional_pathAlgebra_iff_isAcyclic

**Finite-dimensionality of the path algebra is acyclicity of the quiver**, the reading of
`TauCeti.module_finite_pathAlgebra_iff_isAcyclic` over a division ring.
description: **Finite-dimensionality of the path algebra and quiver acyclicity.** For a finite quiver $Q$ with finitely many arrows between any two vertices and a division ring $k$, the path algebra of $Q$ over $k$ is finite-dimensional if and only if $Q$ is acyclic.

**The projection `P₁ ↠ S₁` is the identification of the two lines at the source**, read through
`TauCeti.simpleRepSelfEquiv` and `TauCeti.kroneckerProjSrcEquiv`.
description: **Identification of the Source Projection for the Kronecker Representation Sequence.** For a field $k$ and a singleton set $A$, the map induced by the morphism $g$ at the source vertex in the Kronecker Auslander-Reiten sequence, when post-composed with the self-equivalence of the simple representation at the source, is equal to the natural equivalence identifying the indecomposable projective representation at the source with the simple representation at the source.

name: TauCeti.kroneckerLineRepScalar_intertwine
signature:
theorem TauCeti.kroneckerLineRepScalar_intertwine : ∀ {k : Type u} [inst : Field k] {A : Type v} {a₁ : A} {c d : k} [Nontrivial A]
  (e : TauCeti.kroneckerLineRep k a₁ c ⟶ TauCeti.kroneckerLineRep k a₁ d),
  c * TauCeti.kroneckerLineRepScalar e = d * TauCeti.kroneckerLineRepScalar e
docstring:
**On a quiver carrying more than one arrow the scalars of the two lines agree on the scalar of
any morphism between them**, by naturality along the distinguished arrow. The hypothesis
`Nontrivial A` is the existence of an arrow other than the distinguished one: it forces the two
components of the morphism to agree.
description: **Scalar Agreement for Kronecker Line Representations.** For a quiver with at least two arrows, any morphism between two Kronecker line representations (associated with the same distinguished arrow but potentially different scalars $c$ and $d$) forces the scalars to satisfy the relation $c \cdot s = d \cdot s$, where $s$ is the scalar component of the morphism. In particular, if the quiver is nontrivial, the naturality of the morphism along the arrows ensures that the two scalars $c$ and $d$ must agree on the value of the morphism's underlying scalar.

name: Rep.simple_iff_isIrreducible
signature:
theorem Rep.simple_iff_isIrreducible : ∀ {k : Type u} {G : Type v} [inst : Field k] [inst_1 : Monoid G] (A : Rep.{w, u, v} k G),
  CategoryTheory.Simple A ↔ A.ρ.IsIrreducible
docstring:
**An object of `Rep k G` is simple exactly when the representation it carries is
irreducible.** Both sides say that the `k[G]`-module the object carries is simple: the left-hand
side across `Rep.equivalenceModuleMonoidAlgebra`, the right-hand side across
`Representation.irreducible_iff_isSimpleModule_asModule`.
description: **Equivalence of Simple and Irreducible Representations.** For a representation $A$ of a monoid $G$ over a field $k$, $A$ is a simple object in the category of representations $\text{Rep}(k, G)$ if and only if the representation $A.\rho$ is irreducible.

name: TauCeti.spechtModule_ones_ρ_apply
signature:
theorem TauCeti.spechtModule_ones_ρ_apply : ∀ (n : ℕ) (σ : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (x : ↑(TauCeti.spechtModule (TauCeti.Nat.Partition.ones n)).V),
  ((TauCeti.spechtModule (TauCeti.Nat.Partition.ones n)).ρ σ) x = ↑↑(Equiv.Perm.sign σ) • x
docstring:
**`S^{(1ⁿ)}` is the sign representation**: the symmetric group acts on it through the sign
character.  The sign is unchanged by the relabelling `Fin n ≃ Fin (diagramOf (1ⁿ)).card` that
`TauCeti.spechtModule` transports along.

This is not a `simp` lemma, for the reason given at
`TauCeti.spechtModule_indiscrete_ρ_apply`.
description: **The Specht module of the partition $(1^n)$ is the sign representation.** For any natural number $n$, the action of the symmetric group $S_n$ on the Specht module $S^{(1^n)}$ is given by the sign character. Specifically, for any permutation $\sigma \in S_n$ and any element $x$ in the module, the representation $\rho(\sigma)$ maps $x$ to $\text{sgn}(\sigma) \cdot x$.

name: TauCeti.youngSubgroup

theorem TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.rationalQuotientRingEquiv_quotientMk_weightedX : ∀ {A : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : UniformSpace A] [inst_2 : IsUniformAddGroup A]

description: **Evaluation of the Currying Homeomorphism for Dependent Product Types.** For a family of topological spaces $Y_{i,j}$ indexed by $i \in \iota$ and $j \in \kappa_i$, the homeomorphism between the product space $\prod_{(i, j) \in \sum_{i \in \iota} \kappa_i} Y_{i,j}$ and the iterated product space $\prod_{i \in \iota} \prod_{j \in \kappa_i} Y_{i,j}$ maps a function $f$ to the curried function $(i, j) \mapsto f(i, j)$. Specifically, the value of the homeomorph applied to $f$ at indices $i$ and $j$ is equal to the value of $f$ evaluated at the dependent pair $\langle i, j \rangle$.

name: TauCeti.IsUniformlyLocallyConnected
signature: def TauCeti.IsUniformlyLocallyConnected : {X : Type u_1} → [PseudoMetricSpace X] → Set X → Prop
docstring:
A set `s` is **uniformly locally connected** if for every `ε > 0` there is a `δ > 0` such that
any two points of `s` at distance less than `δ` are joined by a connected subset of `s` of diameter
at most `ε`.

The smallness of the joining set is spelled out as a pairwise distance bound rather than as
`Metric.diam C ≤ ε`, because `Metric.diam` is `0` on an unbounded set, which would let an unbounded
`C` satisfy the condition vacuously. The lemma
`TauCeti.IsUniformlyLocallyConnected.exists_isConnected_diam_le` recovers the diameter phrasing,
boundedness of the joining set being one of its consequences.
description: **Uniformly Locally Connected Set.** A set $s$ in a pseudo-metric space is uniformly locally connected if, for every $\epsilon > 0$, there exists a $\delta > 0$ such that any two points in $s$ with distance less than $\delta$ are contained in a connected subset of $s$ where the distance between any two points in that subset is at most $\epsilon$.
